input.strategy_title: GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Platform teams fund shared GPU clusters but cannot attribute consumption to the
projects using them, so capacity costs are socialized and heavy users have no
incentive to release resources. The in-flight metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is delivering per-project GPU-hour usage data; this strategy
builds the administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of that data. The
metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until that
strategy lands — reporting work here consumes it, and must not re-implement
collection.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API for finance tooling. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- The metering collection pipeline itself (RHAISTRAT-9990)
- Currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars

## Open Questions

1. The metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report
   implementation consuming it carries that external timing risk.

# Expose per-project Kueue quota data for chargeback reporting

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project Kueue quota data surface that administrator
chargeback reporting can consume. Platform administrators need to see GPU
consumption against each project's Kueue quota; Kueue (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue
quota model) is owned by the Distributed Workloads component, and the Dashboard
— which renders the admin views — owns no data plane and reads
component-provided data. This epic makes each project's quota figure
retrievable for reporting, building on Kueue's existing quota model and
metrics exposure. It involves no metering collection: per-project GPU-hour
usage data is delivered by the separate in-flight metering strategy and is out
of scope here.

## Scope

- Expose per-project Kueue quota figures (derived from the
  ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model) in a form the administrator reporting
  views can consume for the current-month window they require.
- Cover every project that holds a Kueue quota; projects without quota are
  reported as such rather than omitted silently.
- Build on the existing Kueue quota model and metrics interfaces; the exposure
  mechanism (metrics extension, API, or aggregated CR reading) is an
  implementation decision for the owning team.
- Out of scope: any metering/usage collection (owned by the separate metering
  strategy), and any Dashboard-side rendering (owned by the Dashboard team).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with a configured Kueue quota, the quota figure surfaced for
  that project matches the configured quota — measured by comparing the
  exposed figure against the ClusterQueue/LocalQueue configuration for a
  sample of projects with differing quota values.
- Every project holding a Kueue quota is retrievable; projects without quota
  are distinguishable from quota-holding projects — measured by enumerating
  projects and verifying none with quota is missing from the exposure.
- The quota data is queryable for current-month reporting at the granularity
  the admin view requires — measured by a successful retrieval covering all
  quota-holding projects in a test cluster.
- No changes are made to metering/usage collection — measured by the metering
  pipeline's configuration and code remaining untouched by this epic's
  changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1, partial — enabling)**: "The Dashboard admin view shows
  current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota" — this epic
  delivers the quota-data half of HLR-3 (the Kueue quota side); the
  admin-view rendering is delivered by the Dashboard epic that consumes this
  data.

# Administrator GPU-hour consumption reports with CSV export and reporting API

## Description

This epic delivers the core administrator-facing chargeback reporting
capability: per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by the separate in-flight
metering strategy, rendered in the Dashboard's administrator view. It also
delivers export of those reports as CSV and retrieval via a stable API for
finance tooling. This epic consumes the metering data — it must not
re-implement collection, which is owned by the metering strategy.

## Scope

- Administrator report view in the Dashboard listing per-project GPU-hour
  consumption for a selectable time range, computed from the delivered
  metering data.
- CSV export of the report for the selected time range.
- A stable retrieval API over the same report data, suitable for finance
  tooling integration, with a documented contract.
- Reading and aggregating the metering data as delivered by the metering
  strategy (the per-project GPU-hour usage data source); no collection
  pipeline logic.
- Out of scope: currency/cost-rate modelling (reports are in GPU-hours, not
  dollars), the metering collection pipeline itself, and Kueue quota
  comparison (delivered by the quota-comparison view built on this reporting
  surface).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given metered per-project GPU-hour usage, an administrator can generate a
  report for any selectable time range listing per-project GPU-hour
  consumption — measured by comparing report totals per project against the
  metering source totals for the same range and projects.
- The report can be exported as CSV — measured by the CSV contents matching
  the on-screen report for the same time range and project set.
- The report data is retrievable via a stable API with a documented contract
  — measured by a finance-tooling-style client retrieving a report for a time
  range through the API and receiving the same figures as the view.
- Report computation consumes the metering data as delivered by the metering
  strategy — measured by the epic introducing no usage-collection logic (the
  metering pipeline remains the sole collector).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: "Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption
  reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data
  delivered by" the metering strategy — direct cover.
- **HLR-2 (P1, bundled)**: "Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via
  a stable API for finance tooling" — bundled into this epic rather than
  split: CSV export and the retrieval API are presentation modes of the same
  per-project report surface and data access built for HLR-1, so a separate
  epic would rebuild the same surface and is not separately schedulable. Epic
  priority remains P0 from HLR-1.

## Risks / Notes

- **External timing risk**: the metering data schema is owned by the in-flight
  metering strategy and finalizes only when that strategy lands. Field
  mapping and GPU-hour semantics may shift until then; this epic's
  implementation consumes the schema as delivered. This schedule constraint
  is externally controlled and cannot be compressed here — if the final
  schema cannot support per-project attribution over time ranges, this epic's
  computation layer requires rework.
- **API-placement assumption**: the strategy does not state where the
  "stable API for finance tooling" (HLR-2) lives. Per `dashboard.md`, the
  Dashboard owns no data plane and its interfaces are the Kubernetes API;
  this epic therefore assumes the retrieval API is delivered with the
  Dashboard reporting surface it builds. Conditional split trigger: if
  review locates the finance-facing API in a backend component instead,
  this epic splits into a Dashboard report-view epic plus a backend API
  epic.

# Admin view of current-month consumption against Kueue quota

## Description

This epic delivers the Dashboard administrator view showing each project's
current-month GPU-hour consumption against its Kueue quota. It builds on two
existing surfaces: the per-project consumption reporting surface delivered by
the administrator reports capability (which this epic extends rather than
duplicates) and the per-project Kueue quota data exposure delivered by the
Distributed Workloads component.

## Scope

- Current-month view in the Dashboard admin surface showing, per project,
  GPU-hour consumption alongside that project's Kueue quota.
- Consumption figures sourced from the same per-project metering-data
  reporting surface used by the consumption reports (no separate consumption
  data access is built).
- Quota figures sourced from the per-project Kueue quota data exposure.
- Projects without a Kueue quota are presented distinctly (consumption shown,
  quota marked absent) rather than dropped from the view.
- Out of scope: metering collection, quota data exposure itself, CSV/API
  export, and currency/cost-rate modelling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the current calendar month, the admin view shows each project's
  consumption against its Kueue quota — measured by comparing displayed
  figures against the metering-source consumption totals and the configured
  Kueue quotas for a sample of projects.
- Quota figures displayed match the configured Kueue quotas — measured by
  reconciling the view's quota column against ClusterQueue/LocalQueue
  configuration for quota-holding projects.
- Projects without quota are visibly distinguishable from quota-holding
  projects — measured by a project with consumption but no quota appearing
  with an explicit no-quota indication rather than being omitted.
- The view consumes the existing per-project consumption reporting surface
  rather than re-implementing consumption data access — measured by the epic
  introducing no independent metering-data query path.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: "The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption
  against each project's Kueue quota" — direct cover (quota-data side enabled
  by the Distributed Workloads quota exposure; rendering delivered here).

## Risks / Notes

- **External timing risk**: consumption figures derive from the metering data
  delivered by the in-flight metering strategy, whose schema finalizes only
  when that strategy lands — externally controlled timing that cannot be
  compressed here; consumption semantics may shift until then.

# Document report semantics and export integration

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator documentation for GPU chargeback
reporting: what the reports mean (in particular what counts as a GPU-hour),
how time ranges are interpreted, and how finance tooling integrates with the
CSV export and the reporting API. It documents the capability as built, which
is why it is scheduled after all implementation epics.

## Scope

Content outline (authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- **Report semantics topic**: what counts as a GPU-hour in the chargeback
  reports, aligned with the metering semantics delivered by the metering
  strategy; how per-project attribution and selectable time ranges are
  interpreted; how quota comparison in the admin view is computed.
- **Export and integration guide**: retrieving reports as CSV and via the
  stable reporting API, aimed at finance tooling consumers; the API contract
  as delivered.
- **Administrator task flow**: viewing per-project consumption reports and
  the current-month consumption-versus-quota view in the Dashboard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers report semantics including an explicit definition of
  what counts as a GPU-hour, consistent with the metering data semantics as
  delivered — measured by review against the landed reporting and metering
  behavior.
- Export integration (CSV and reporting API) is documented for finance
  tooling consumers — measured by a reader being able to retrieve a report
  via CSV and the API using only the documentation.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  reporting capability by engineering — measured by recorded technical review
  sign-off before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: "Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a
  GPU-hour) and export integration" — direct cover. Epic priority is P1 per
  the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority Major → P1), not
  inherited from HLR-4.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9018 (GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators)

Strategy status: Refinement Done, priority Major. The strategy builds
administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of per-project GPU-hour metering
data delivered by the in-flight strategy RHAISTRAT-9990 (external dependency,
schema owned there and not final until that strategy lands).

## Strategy Parsing Notes

- The strategy provides HLRs (HLR-1..HLR-4) and an Affected Components list
  (Dashboard, Distributed Workloads) but **no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, and no NFRs**.
  Owner teams were inferred from `.context/architecture-context/` (RHOAI
  Dashboard owns Dashboard; Distributed Workloads owns Distributed Workloads);
  epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs. Recorded as health
  warnings below.
- No Staff Engineer Input section is present — no overrides to log.
- Both affected components exist in the platform (architecture context files
  `dashboard.md` and `distributed-workloads.md` under
  `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/`), so no onboarding
  chain (repo/license/konflux) is needed; both are Konflux-onboarded already.

## Open Question Handling (no Investigation epic)

The strategy's single open question states that the metering data schema
finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands and that report implementation
"carries that external timing risk." Applying the decision rule — does the
answer change which downstream epics exist or what they do? — **no**: the
reporting view, export/API, quota comparison, and documentation epics exist and
deliver the same capability regardless of the schema's final field layout; the
schema shapes field mapping inside those epics (an implementation detail the
consuming team resolves), and the timing is a schedule risk controlled by an
external party. The unknown is therefore NOT a genuine unknown warranting an
Investigation epic. It is modeled as:

- an **external precondition** recorded in the Risks/Notes of the consuming
  epics (RHAISTRAT-9990 is a separate strategy — there is no epic in this
  decomposition to draw a DAG edge to), and
- **acceptance criteria on the consuming epics** phrased at the engineering
  completion point they control (reports computed from the metering data as
  delivered).

This also means no conditional branches: the outcome cannot add or remove epics
in this plan.

| RHAISTRAT-9018-E001 | Expose per-project Kueue quota data for chargeback reporting | Implementation | Distributed Workloads | Distributed Workloads | P1 |
